title: Rework Terraform modules to support per-cluster state backends and GPU subpool topology
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Private installs were using a single monolithic state layout and a single GPU nodepool definition which made multi-cluster deployments and controlled rolling upgrades for GPU-backed workloads brittle. This PR splits state backends by cluster/environment and introduces a first-class GPU subpool abstraction so customers can define multiple heterogeneous GPU pools (e.g. nvidia-a100-40g, nvidia-t4) with taints/affinity and separate autoscaling profiles.

What changed (high-level):
- Introduced module 'cluster-state' to encapsulate backend configuration and locking per-cluster. Supports S3+Dynamo for AWS, GCS+locks for GCP, and local file backend for on-prem dry-runs.
- Added 'gpu-subpool' reusable module that exposes node selector labels, taints, max/min sizes, and per-subpool IAM bindings where applicable.
- Refactored the top-level private deployment module to compose multiple gpu-subpool instances and to reference the per-cluster state backend.
- Added a state migration helper (scripts/migrate_state.sh) and documentation for migrating existing single-state deployments to per-cluster states.
- Updated examples/ to include a two-subpool production example and a single-subpool dev example.

Migration steps for operators:
1) Review generated plan for cluster-state module in a non-production copy of your state bucket.
2) Run scripts/migrate_state.sh --source-bucket <old> --dest-prefix <cluster>/ to split state into cluster-specific prefixes.
3) Apply terraform in each cluster order (control plane first, then GPU pools) following the README.

Rollback plan:
- If migration introduces an error, the script keeps a timestamped copy of the original state and will not delete it. Re-point the backend to the original prefix and apply the previous module version.

Testing and validation:
- Local plan/unit tests with terratest mock infra run in CI.
- Manual validation runs were performed against a GKE dev project and an AWS VPC staging account, confirming nodepool creation, taint/affinity application, and IAM bindings for GPU pools.

Notes and follow-ups:
- This PR intentionally does not change default behavior for fresh installs (defaults remain single cluster state unless cluster_state module invoked).
- We should add an automated migration job in the private-installer flow in a follow-up PR to orchestrate migration for customers on upgrade.

Checklist: 
- [x] Module code and docs
- [x] Migration script and README
- [x] Example configs (dev/prod)
- [x] CI terratest coverage

Refs: Linear ENG-1124, INFRA-938, related PRs in redwood-private-installer for orchestration
